teaching: Teaching values for a two-group diffusion model with homogenised cells. Not evaluated nuclear data; not for design or safety analysis.

sources.lamarsh: J.R. Lamarsh, A.J. Baratta, Introduction to Nuclear Engineering, 3rd ed., Prentice Hall 2001: Tables 5.2, 5.3, 7.5 and the 2200 m/s data of Table II.2
sources.iaea2d: IAEA 2-D PWR benchmark, ANL-7416 Supplement 2 (1977), problem 11-A2
sources.orpheus: ORPHEUS teaching code, theory manual, reactor kinetics (docs/research/2664/chemistry.md, source 31)
sources.ijs: TRIGA reactor simulator physics manual, Jozef Stefan Institute (docs/research/2664/chemistry.md, source 28)
sources.nubase: NUBASE2020: F.G. Kondev et al., Chinese Physics C 45 (2021) 030001
sources.tk: N.E. Todreas, M.S. Kazimi, Nuclear Systems I, decay heat after long operation P/P0 = 0.066 t^-0.2
sources.derived: computed by scripts/chem/build_xs2g.py from the cited inputs
sources.teaching: chosen for this teaching model; see the note of the entry

groups.note: v2: mean speed of a Maxwellian at 293 K (2/sqrt(pi) times 2200 m/s), grows with the square root of the moderator temperature; v1: chosen so the slowing-down time 1/(v1 Sigma_s12) is 8 microseconds in water and 0.12 ms in graphite

poisons.note: Yields per fission of U-235 by thermal neutrons; the absorption cross-sections are thermal averages used as they are (no 1/v correction).

decayHeat.note: Non-negative least-squares fit of 0.066 t^-0.2 by exponential groups on 1 s to 1e8 s (relative error fitError). The sum of a is the decay-heat share of the power in equilibrium.

materials.note: Uranium metal rod in an otherwise empty channel: 2 % of the cell is uranium (0.711 wt% U-235). Thermal: Maxwellian averages of the 2200 m/s data divided by a self-shielding factor 1.4 (a rod of about 3 cm), plus 1.5e-4 /cm for can, air and impurities. Fast: U-238 resonance capture with an effective resonance integral of 10 b over the lethargy 18.2, fast fission of U-238 with 0.04 b, epithermal U-235 fission 12 b and capture 6 b. D (1.6 and 2.0 cm) chosen between a moderator and a cavity: the channel is mostly empty. For lattices with a large pitch (about 20 cm) in graphite or heavy water.

UO2 rod bundle without moderator: 45 % of the cell is UO2, 12 % zircaloy; enrichment adjustable from 0.72 to 5 wt% (reference 3 %). Thermal: Maxwellian averages divided by a self-shielding factor 1.1. Fast: effective resonance integral 20 b, fast fission of U-238 0.10 b, epithermal U-235 fission 12 b and capture 6 b. For tight lattices (pitch of 1 to 2 cm) with light water.

H2O at 293 K (Lamarsh Tables 5.2 and 5.3); fast absorption neglected. Density with temperature by a quadratic fit to pressurised liquid water, 1 - 2.0e-4 dT - 2.6e-6 dT^2 (dT above 293 K; 0.73 at 580 K); the Sigmas follow the density and the void fraction, D its inverse, thermal absorption also 1/v.
D2O with 0.25 % H2O at 293 K (Lamarsh Tables 5.2 and 5.3); the same density fit as light water.
Reactor graphite, 1.60 g/cm3, at 293 K (Lamarsh Tables 5.2 and 5.3); thermal absorption 1/v with its temperature.
Type 304: thermal absorption from the 2200 m/s cross-sections of Fe, Cr and Ni (2.56, 3.1, 4.5 b) and their number densities; reflector and structure.
Zirconium, 0.0429 atoms per barn cm, absorption 0.185 b, scattering 6.4 b.

Effective values of a homogenised rod cell: a real B4C rod is black to thermal neutrons, which diffusion theory cannot represent; 0.40 /cm makes a fully inserted cell strongly absorbing. Scale: the rodded assembly of the IAEA benchmark adds 0.045 /cm with rods in about a tenth of its area.
Effective values of a homogenised rod cell: weaker than B4C for thermal neutrons, stronger above (resonances of indium and silver).
A pressure tube with light-water coolant: 50 % water, 10 % zircaloy, 40 % gap (volume-weighted Sigmas, 1/D weighted). The water part follows the coolant temperature and void.
An empty cell. Neutrons stream through a cavity without collisions, which diffusion theory does not describe; a large diffusion coefficient (5 cm) stands in for it.
A start-up source in a small steel capsule. The source strength is a property of the reactor document (neutrons per second); the cell itself is a weak absorber.
